issues.body: _alert_route computes one token as ALERT_TOKEN or REGISTRY_ALERT_TOKEN and returns that same token even when a same-repo/public/unverifiable ALERT_REPO is rejected. Thus ALERT_REPO=private/alerts, ALERT_TOKEN scoped only to that private repo, and a failed visibility probe yields (REGISTRY_REPO, ALERT_TOKEN), not (REGISTRY_REPO, REGISTRY_ALERT_TOKEN). The registry write then lacks permission. This is especially serious here because _ops_alert is deliberately best-effort and catches delivery errors, so the operational failure proceeds with no alert despite the new docstring's claim that fallback loses no alert. The new assertions expecting (reg/repo, t1) make the credential-routing bug pass the self-test.
issues.fix_hint: Keep the private-route token and registry fallback token separate. Probe and write a confirmed private ALERT_REPO with ALERT_TOKEN; for every rejected/unconfigured route return REGISTRY_REPO with REGISTRY_ALERT_TOKEN (or the intended ambient registry credential). Update the rejection and same-repo tests to use distinct sentinel tokens and assert that fallback uses the registry sentinel, while the visibility probe alone uses the alert sentinel.
issues.title: Rejected private routes fall back to the registry with the wrong token

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The plan/groom visibility routing is fail-closed and has end-to-end coverage, but worker-pr's newly added rejection fallback binds the registry destination to the private-route credential. In the common case where ALERT_TOKEN is scoped only to ALERT_REPO, the fallback cannot write and _ops_alert swallows the failure, contradicting the change's no-alert-lost guarantee. The self-test currently codifies this wrong credential choice. One major issue requires changes.
